ideas.hypothesis: Chinese provinces that scored higher on a new-type (informatization-led) industrialization index before 2008 were more resilient to the 2008-09 global trade collapse: their export and industrial output fell less and recovered faster. Informatization therefore acts as a buffer against globalization shocks and is a research priority for regional policy.

sources.role: measure: factor-analytic index of the new-type industrialization level in China's western region
measure/mechanism: regional economic resilience concepts (resistance and recovery)
mechanism: industrialization led by informatization as China's development path
mechanism: IT infusion supports global business strategy and adaptability
method: a structured research-and-data-needs agenda for digital technologies

ideas.test: Provincial panel for 2003-2012 from statistical yearbooks. Construct the factor-analytic index for 2007, then measure resistance (peak-to-trough fall in exports and industrial value added, 2008-09) and recovery (rebound by 2011). Regress both on the 2007 index, controlling for export intensity, FDI share and the coastal dummy.
ideas.disconfirming: The pre-crisis index does not predict smaller declines or faster recovery once export exposure is controlled, or high-index provinces were hit harder.

ideas.hypothesis: Cities that take part in international knowledge-sharing and benchmarking networks (such as EU-funded good-practice exchanges) open new tramway or BRT systems sooner than comparable non-participating cities, so cross-border policy transfer speeds up the global diffusion of urban rail.

sources.role: mechanism/setting: benchmarking and good-practice sharing across Europe, Asia and Latin America
measure: annual worldwide counts and forecasts of new tramway openings
method: mapping the scientific research context of BRT applications
method: content analysis of a research literature to identify gaps
method: a critique of case-study methods for openness-growth links, guiding a multi-city event-history design

ideas.test: Build a city-year panel (2000-2019) of medium and large cities with tram or BRT opening dates coded from trade-press annual reviews, and membership in international transport knowledge networks or projects. Estimate a Cox hazard model of first opening on membership, controlling for population, GDP per capita and national rail policy.
ideas.disconfirming: Network membership has no association with time to opening, or members adopt only after peers in the same country, which points to national rather than international diffusion.

ideas.hypothesis: The post-disaster gradient found in New Orleans, where building permits cluster near fixed streetcar stops after the shock, replicates in other disaster-struck cities with fixed rail in different national institutional settings. The rail-proximity development premium is therefore not specific to the U.S. context.

sources.role: method: post-Katrina permit frequency by distance to streetcar stops, controlling for damage and pre-shock conditions
mechanism: macro-financial conditions (lagged policy rate) as a control for real-estate demand
method: demand forecasting that combines perceived and empirical information
setting: international catalogue of light-rail and tram systems to select replication cities
setting: an Asian urban-logistics context illustrating cross-country transfer of urban transport findings

ideas.test: Apply the New Orleans specification (permits by distance band to rail stops, with damage and pre-shock controls) to geocoded permit or consent data from one or two non-U.S. disaster cities that had operating tram or light rail during the recovery. Compare the distance-decay coefficients across cities.
ideas.disconfirming: No permit gradient near rail stops after the disaster in the replication cities, or a gradient that is opposite in sign.

ideas.hypothesis: Pharmaceutical sponsors that innovate persistently (continuous patenting) place a larger share of their trial sites in emerging regions such as Latin America. Trials run there include a local pharmacoeconomic component less often than trials run at home, which leaves an evidence gap that grows as trials globalize.

sources.role: mechanism/setting: pitfalls and potential of pharmacoeconomic components in Latin American trials
measure: innovation persistence measured from patent continuity at the firm level
measure: industry updates on approvals and trial news by sponsor
method: linking datasets across domains for better policy
method: analysing research trends and how research supply matches need

ideas.test: Draw a sample of about 500 phase III trials (2005-2019) from a trial registry with site countries and sponsors. Link sponsors to patent counts to code persistence, and code whether the protocol or publication includes a cost or economic endpoint. Regress the share of Latin American sites on persistence, and the presence of an economic endpoint on site region.
ideas.disconfirming: Persistent innovators do not offshore more, or Latin American-sited trials include economic endpoints as often as home-country trials.

ideas.hypothesis: Within China's lagging zones (the western region and the Beibu Gulf), prefectures whose FDI and exports grew faster after the regional development programmes started converged faster toward coastal zones on the new-type industrialization index. Openness explains more of the convergence than gains in human resources do.

sources.role: measure: dynamic factor-analytic index of new-type industrialization under the western development strategy
finding/setting: a persistent or widening gap between the Beibu Gulf and developed economic zones
mechanism: regional resilience and adaptive capacity in regional development

ideas.test: Prefecture-level panel (2000-2015) that rebuilds the index each year. Estimate beta-convergence regressions of index growth on the initial gap to the coastal mean, interacted with FDI/GDP and export/GDP growth and with tertiary-education growth, and compare the partial R-squared of the openness and education terms.
ideas.disconfirming: Openness growth does not speed convergence, or education growth accounts for most of it.

ideas.hypothesis: Evaluations of transport interventions that use validated quality-of-life instruments from clinical trials (generic health-related quality of life plus well-being scales) detect effects of traffic calming or town-centre redesign on residents' well-being that are missed by appraisals based on travel time. Because the instruments are standardized, the effects can be compared across countries.

sources.role: method/measure: choosing and using quality-of-life instruments in trials
mechanism: a well-designed traffic environment contributes to well-being and belonging
setting: policy dilemmas of mobility-dependent societies
measure: cross-country social well-being indices
setting: transport-environment policy evaluation in Sweden

ideas.test: Controlled before-after study of one traffic-calming or redesign scheme: survey about 300 residents in treated and matched control streets with EQ-5D and a validated well-being scale before and 12 months after, together with the usual travel-time and traffic-count data. Estimate difference-in-differences on the well-being scores.
ideas.disconfirming: Well-being scores change no more on treated streets than on control streets, even where traffic counts fell substantially.

ideas.hypothesis: Tram and light-rail lines whose interchange nodes are integrated with the surrounding urban fabric have smaller ridership shortfalls against forecast. The effect is larger in Global South cities that import system designs from abroad, where forecasts rely on transferred assumptions and lower-quality data.

sources.role: mechanism: success depends on integration of the node with the urban environment and culture
setting: coordinated metropolitan planning of tramway and rail extensions
method: designing evaluation into a project from the start, as in trials
method caveat: data-quality pitfalls in big-data spatial analysis
measure: trajectory-based assessment of service reliability in a Global South city

ideas.test: Compile forecast and actual opening-year ridership for 30-40 tram and light-rail lines across countries. Code a node-integration index for each (land-use mix within 400 m, walk connectivity, transfer distances) and a Global South dummy, then regress log(actual/forecast) on the index and its interaction with the dummy.
ideas.disconfirming: Integration is unrelated to the forecast shortfall, or its effect is no larger in Global South cities.

ideas.hypothesis: Place-based investment incentives such as Opportunity Zones mostly draw capital into real estate rather than R&D-intensive establishments. In New Orleans, designated tracts see more real-estate and construction entry but no rise in knowledge-intensive firms compared with eligible tracts that were not designated, consistent with the view that productivity gains come from research capacity rather than tax incentives alone.

sources.role: setting/mechanism: Opportunity Zones in New Orleans as an investment incentive aimed at housing and development
finding: different R&D types, basic research among them, have different effects on productivity growth
mechanism: basic research capacity (Bell Labs) depends on institutional structure, not market incentives alone
mechanism: regional disparities persist under uniform policy frameworks
method: before-after assessment of a policy regime change (FTA)

ideas.test: Use establishment-level business register data for Louisiana census tracts, 2014-2021. Compare designated with eligible-but-not-designated tracts in a difference-in-differences of new establishments by sector (real estate/construction versus NAICS R&D-intensive industries), with New Orleans as the focal case and other Louisiana metros as robustness checks.
ideas.disconfirming: Designated tracts show significant growth in R&D-intensive establishment entry comparable to real-estate entry.

ideas.hypothesis: Physicians paid more through procedure-based fee-for-service consider patients' out-of-pocket costs less often than nonprocedural and primary care physicians. Across countries, the share of physicians who report considering patient cost-sharing is higher where pay is less procedure-weighted.

sources.role: measure/finding: nationally representative physician survey on considering patients' out-of-pocket costs
mechanism: income gaps between procedural and nonprocedural specialties
measure: median compensation trends by provider type
method: systematic review comparing provider ownership types on performance

ideas.test: (1) Within the U.S., link physician survey responses on cost consideration to specialty-level procedural revenue shares and regress cost consideration on procedural share. (2) Cross-nationally, use an international physician survey with a comparable item and code each country's payment mix (fee-for-service share) as a country-level predictor.
ideas.disconfirming: Procedural share and fee-for-service intensity are unrelated to how often physicians consider out-of-pocket costs, once practice setting is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Revenue-management concepts spread from transport (rail and airline yield pricing) into the healthcare practice-management literature with a lag of several years. Within a country, the volume of practice-management publications on demand-based pricing and scheduling follows earlier growth in transport publications on yield management.

sources.role: mechanism: transfer of the yield-system pricing model to Chinese rail
setting: practice-management literature on revenue growth
mechanism: market research taking a growing role in transit
measure: performance-based accountability metrics as an outcome of research adoption
method: empirical analysis of research topic trends and users

ideas.test: Bibliometric time series (1990-2019) counting articles that mention yield or revenue management in transport and in healthcare management journals, by country of the first author. Estimate cross-lagged and Granger causality models between the two series, pooled and by country.
ideas.disconfirming: Healthcare publications do not lag transport publications, or the two series move together contemporaneously with no lead-lag structure.
